answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (15.5.2024) The primary responsibility for education lies with Member States and the national authorities will have to decide on the use of digital technologies, such as artificial intelligence (AI), in education according to the relevant circumstances.

There is no EU legislation mandating an authorisation to use AI in higher education, hence the concept of unauthorised use is not applicable. However, the use of AI in higher education must respect all horizontally applicable EU legislation, including the General Data Protection Regulation1.

The forthcoming AI Act2 lists AI systems in education and vocational training in Annex III, point 3, among the high-risk systems that will be subject to heightened requirements. In particular, ‘AI systems intended to be used for monitoring and detecting prohibited behaviour of students during tests in the context of/within education and vocational training institutions’ fall within this category.

Those systems will have to fulfil the quality criteria set out in the AI Act and to carry out ex-ante conformity assessments. Moreover, the use of AI systems to infer emotions of a natural person in education institutions will be expressly prohibited under the AI Act, except for medical or safety reasons.

It should be noted that it is not the objective of the AI Act to limit the use of AI, but to ensure that AI systems are designed and deployed in such a way so as to be beneficial to society and to mitigate risks to the fundamental rights of the persons on whom they are deployed. Regarding AI use in teaching and learning, ethical guidelines have been prepared for educators3.
1 https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj 2 Regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on laying down harmonised rules on Artificial

Intelligence (Artificial Intelligence Act) and amending certain Union Legislative Acts (COM(2021)0206). 3 https://education.ec.europa.eu/news/ethical-guidelines-on-the-use-of-artificial-intelligence-and-data-inteaching-and-learning-for-educators
